title: Recovery is available through Time Travel point-in-time recovery and through a scheduled export to a portable artifact
description: Recovery has two paths, both configured in the project. Path one: Time Travel, the vendor's built-in point-in-time recovery, invoked via `wrangler d1 time-travel restore <database> --timestamp=<unix-seconds>`; the recovery window is the vendor's supported window at the project's plan tier. Path two: a scheduled `wrangler d1 export <database> --output=<artifact> --remote` producing a portable `.sql` artifact written to a project-configured destination (a repository asset, an R2 bucket, an object store the project already runs); the schedule and destination are project-configured. Both paths preserve the schema and rows at the recovery moment; both are exercisable from the CI or ops surface without a Worker code change.
rationale: Time Travel is the natural first line of defence for D1: it is built in, requires no configuration, and covers the operator's likely restore window (accidental drop, bad deploy) inside a bounded lookback. It is not a substitute for a portable dump: the recovery window is finite, the restore is in-place and destructive, and an operator whose compliance model demands off-vendor retention needs the export as well. Naming both paths at the REQ level makes the two-part recovery posture a floor, not a project convention.
